title: How the Moonwalk Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about moonwalking, reading habits, and Stephen King and Dean Koontz, then turn to the history of the moonwalk. They trace precursors such as Cab Calloway's the Buzz, the Camel Walk, Sammy Davis Jr., Marcel Marceau's air walk, and Bill Bailey's 1955 Apollo moonwalk. They credit mimes like Shields and Yarnell and dancers like Jeffrey Daniel, whose backslide inspired Michael Jackson's moonwalk. They describe the 1983 Motown special performance of Billy Jean, the disputed question of who taught Jackson, the popping and locking origins with Rerun and the Electric Boogaloos, and a how-to for the backslide. The episode ends with a correction about the Gettysburg Address episode and a listener mail letter from Trevor on bias in scientific research.

segments.title: Opening banter: moonwalking and books
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about Josh's moonwalk ability, bailing on hard things, reading habits, Sapiens, and Stephen King versus Dean Koontz.

segments.title: Michael Jackson, breakdancing, and early moonwalk precursors
segments.summary: Josh describes his youth listening to music and his interest in breakdancing, noting the moonwalk is a popping move. They discuss Cab Calloway's the Buzz from the 1930s, the Camel Walk, and Sammy Davis Jr. and James Brown.

segments.title: Bill Bailey and the air walk
segments.summary: Bill Bailey's 1955 moonwalk at the Apollo is described, along with Marcel Marceau's air walk, which is floating in place rather than a dance. The hosts note the difficulty of crediting an inventor.

segments.title: Mimes, Shields and Yarnell, and Jeffrey Daniel's backslide
segments.summary: The 1970s mime craze is discussed, including Shields and Yarnell, and why people disliked mimes. Jeffrey Daniel of Shalamar performed the backslide on Soul Train and Solid Gold, inspired by mime, and other dancers worked on it too.

segments.title: Michael Jackson's 1983 Motown special and who taught him
segments.summary: Michael Jackson performed Billy Jean at the Motown Retrospective special and the moonwalk was widely seen for the first time. The hosts discuss who taught Jackson, noting choreographers Jeffrey Daniel, Jeron Casper, and Derek Coolie Jackson, and that Jackson never claimed to invent it.
topics: who taught Michael Jackson the moonwalk

segments.title: Lean, popping and locking origins, and Rerun
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the lean illusion and a tutorial by Robert Hoffman. They cover the Electric Boogaloos and the origins of popping and locking, Don Campbell's locking, and Rerun from What's Happening.

segments.title: How to do the moonwalk (backslide)
segments.summary: Josh walks through how to do the backslide: flat foot dragged back, heel-and-ball switch, long stride, and a snap of both feet. He notes the moonwalk is actually called the backslide and that the illusion depends on the walking appearance.

segments.title: Correction: Gettysburg Address episode
segments.summary: The hosts correct their Gettysburg Address episode, saying they confused total casualties with deaths and misstated the army percentages.

segments.title: Listener mail: research bias
segments.summary: Listener Trevor writes about bias in research, funding pressure, and the difficulty of publishing negative studies.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts give contact information and sign off.
